transcript:
-This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
-Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump was in Texas again today,
trying to rally support for Republican Ken Paxton
Senate campaign against Democrat James Tallarico.
-He's never gonna love me,
and he's never gonna love oil and gas,
and he's never gonna love your Second Amendment,
and he's never gonna love your children the way you do.
It's a different kind of love.
You can't put this guy -- You can't have a vote like that.
It's too close.
-It was Trump's fourth visit to Texas since September,
highlighting the state's importance to Republicans.
Texas has been a Republican stronghold for decades,
but Tallarico's outreach and Paxton's political
and personal struggles have made it a battleground.
More than 34 million ballots have already been cast
during early voting for the midterms,
and we are now just one week away from Election Day
on November 3rd, as NPR's Hansi Luong reports.
-Voters have returned some 18 million mail-in ballots
around the country.
They've also cast about 17 million ballots
in person at early voting sites.
That's according to statistics compiled
by the University of Florida's election lab.
More voters are set to exercise their rights at the polls
before next Tuesday's Election Day.
Early in-person voting starts tomorrow in Oklahoma
and on Thursday in Kentucky.
For mail-in voters, today is the US Postal Service's
recommended deadline for mailing back ballots in states
where they must be received by Election Day.
Voters can also consider returning their mail-in ballot
at their local election office
or at any available ballot drop box.
And if you're eligible to vote in North Carolina's
midterm elections but haven't registered yet,
your last chance is at early voting sites
this Saturday, Halloween.
Hansi Luong, NPR News.
-The US says it will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro
and his family.
Bolsonaro lost Sunday's presidential election runoff
in Brazil and is under investigation
on corruption charges, and PR's Kerry Kahn reports.
-According to a US administration official,
the State Department will issue visas
to Bolsonaro and his family, allowing entry into the US.
In a video released Monday, Bolsonaro said
federal police officials had ordered him
to surrender his passport.
He's facing multiple investigations,
including allegations of money laundering and tax evasion.
He has denied any wrongdoing.
The US has not recognized the results
of Sunday's presidential election,
won by incumbent Luis Anacio Lula da Silva.
Trump did not endorse Bolsonaro,
a close conservative ally, but he has said
the Brazilian elections appeared, quote, "rigged."
At his 81st birthday celebration, Lula said, quote,
"Those who have nothing to hide have nothing to fear."
Kerry Kahn, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
-The Supreme Court has declined to intervene
in a dispute over a Biden-era immigration regulation.
Democratic-led cities sought to revive the rule,
which allowed immigration judges to pause
some deportation proceedings.
They argued it helped crime victims and vulnerable juveniles.
Texas and the Trump administration
had blocked the regulation,
claiming it allowed people to stay indefinitely.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Cornell University says it will review
how it handled the co-ed housing assignment
of a student who returned to campus
after serving a suspension
connected to an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house.
A professor accused the university
of a dangerous disconnect between its disciplinary
and housing systems, saying housing officials
were unaware of the student's history
and his roommate received no warning.
It's been nearly a year since Congress
ended the enhanced premium tax credits
that made Affordable Care Act coverage
cheaper for most Americans in the marketplace.
Now, Georgia is seeking federal approval
for a proposal that could help some who lost
those pandemic-era tax credits from WABE
and Atlanta. Jess Mater has more.
Georgia's proposing a new state tax credit
for its state-run marketplace, Georgia Access.
This makes Georgia among the first states
to try and make up the loss of that federal subsidy.
People who qualify would get it via a new personal account,
which they could then use toward their monthly premiums.
State officials say the proposal is designed
to address rising healthcare costs
and give consumers visibility
into the assistance they receive.
The plan is still awaiting federal review.
If approved, it would take effect in 2028.
For "NPR News," I'm Jess Mater in Atlanta.
Villanova University is deepening its ties
to the Vatican thanks to its famous alumnus Pope Leo.
On Sunday, Villanova's men's and women's basketball teams
will play Notre Dame in Rome.
Villanova has seen a 10% increase in applications
since Pope Leo's elections.
Some school officials call it the Pope Leo effect.
This is "NPR News" from Washington.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone,
offering an alternative approach to language learning.
Without relying on traditional memorization,
the platform guides users
to intuitively think in a second language.
More information at rosettaestone.com.
